text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000181 bills 99215 at roughly three times the risk-adjusted expectation, with elevated rates in every complexity band, but records came back for too few claims to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by panel mix alone. The provider's 99215 share runs well above the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with 0 to 1 conditions. Sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0104645 (back pain only), C0104770 (UTI in an 18-year-old) and C0105873 point the same way. Most 99215 volume, however, sits on patients with 5 or more conditions, as in sampled claims like C0105346 and C0106138, where high-level visits are plausible. The small low-complexity share also limits how much those examples can carry. All 4 documented 99215s were supported at high MDM, which leans toward legitimacy, but four charts out of 728 is far too thin to judge. Four of the nine notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test on the claim, which is weak evidence of cloned or inflated documentation. A reviewer should first request a larger targeted chart sample, prioritizing the 99215s on 0 to 1 condition patients in the claim list, and check those notes for templated or copied MDM and data-review language."}
